questions.prompt: During a routine inspection, a technician discovered that software that was installed on a computer was secretly collecting data about websites that were visited by users of the computer. Which type of threat is affecting this computer?

summary.text: Spyware covertly collects information about user activity.

concept.text: Spyware covertly collects information about user activity. Classify the behaviour described before considering a possible later consequence such as identity theft.

rationale.text: A DoS attack targets service availability; no disruption is described.
Identity theft is misuse of someone's identity. Collecting browsing history does not by itself establish that misuse.
Secretly monitoring websites visited is characteristic spyware behaviour.
Zero-day describes exploitation of a vulnerability before an effective fix is available; the prompt gives no information about an exploit.

sourceExplanation.text: Spyware is software that is installed on a network device and that collects information.

questions.prompt: Which term refers to a network that provides secure access to the corporate offices by suppliers, customers and collaborators?

summary.text: An extranet gives authorised outsiders controlled access to an organisation's resources.

concept.text: An extranet gives authorised outsiders controlled access to an organisation's resources. The distinction is the intended audience, not whether access uses an Internet connection.

rationale.text: The Internet is the global interconnection of networks, not a company's restricted partner-access environment.
An intranet primarily serves internal organisational users.
An extranet supports controlled access for suppliers, customers and collaborators.
Extendednet is not the standard network term for this arrangement.

sourceExplanation.text: The term Internet refers to the worldwide collection of connected networks. Intranet refers to a private connection of LANs and WANS that belong to an organization and is designed to be accessible to the members of the organization, employees, or others with authorization. Extranets provide secure and safe access to suppliers, customers, and collaborators. Extendednet is not a type of network.

questions.prompt: A large corporation has modified its network to allow users to access network resources from their personal laptops and smart phones. Which networking trend does this describe?

summary.text: BYOD means bring your own device: employees use personally owned equipment to access organisational resources.

concept.text: BYOD means bring your own device: employees use personally owned equipment to access organisational resources. Ownership and access policy are the decisive clues.

rationale.text: Cloud computing describes remotely provided computing resources, not who owns the user's laptop.
Online collaboration describes working together using network services, regardless of device ownership.
Personal laptops and smartphones accessing corporate resources are the defining BYOD scenario.
Video conferencing is a communication application; the scenario does not mention a video meeting.

sourceExplanation.text: BYOD allows end users to use personal tools to access the corporate network. Allowing this trend can have major impacts on a network, such as security and compatibility with corporate software and devices.

questions.prompt: What is an ISP?

options.text: It is a standards body that develops cabling and wiring standards for networking.
It is a protocol that establishes how computers within a local network communicate.
It is an organization that enables individuals and businesses to connect to the Internet.
It is a networking device that combines the functionality of several different networking devices in one.

summary.text: An Internet service provider supplies Internet connectivity to customers.

concept.text: An Internet service provider supplies Internet connectivity to customers. Its role differs from a standards organisation, a protocol, or a piece of equipment.

rationale.text: Standards bodies define technical specifications; that does not make them connectivity providers.
A protocol is a set of communication rules, not an organisation selling access.
Providing Internet access to individuals and businesses is the ISP's role.
An integrated networking device combines functions such as routing and switching; it is equipment rather than a provider organisation.

sourceExplanation.text: An ISP, or Internet Service Provider, is an organization that provides access to the Internet for businesses and individuals.

questions.prompt: Match the requirements of a reliable network with the supporting network architecture. (Not all options are used.)

prompts.text: fault tolerance
security
scalability

choices.text: Protect the network from unauthorized access.
Match the type of communication with a specific priority.
Expand the network without degrading the service for existing users.
Ensure that streaming data is provided over high speed links.

summary.text: Match each architecture characteristic to its supporting requirement.

concept.text: Match each architecture characteristic to its supporting requirement. The two unused requirements are retained as distractors; no QoS category has been invented.

rationale.text: Redundant links and devices provide alternate paths or components after a failure. Traffic priority concerns QoS rather than redundancy.
Preventing unauthorised access is a security objective. High-speed links do not themselves authenticate users or control permissions.
Adding users or capacity without degrading existing service is scalability. The two unused statements concern traffic treatment or streaming capacity rather than this growth property.

editorialNotes.originalText: Three category tokens assigned into five description slots
editorialNotes.revisedText: Three category prompts and five description choices
editorialNotes.reason: Equivalent orientation avoids unexplained empty source slots and retains both distractors.

questions.prompt: An employee at a branch office is creating a quote for a customer. In order to do this, the employee needs to access confidential pricing information from internal servers at the Head Office. What type of network would the employee access?

summary.text: An intranet supports private organisational access across one or many locations.

concept.text: An intranet supports private organisational access across one or many locations. A branch employee consulting headquarters resources is an internal-access scenario.

rationale.text: The employee is accessing internal organisational information, which fits an intranet.
The connection might traverse the Internet, but that does not make the confidential internal service a public Internet resource.
An extranet is aimed at authorised external partners; the person described is an employee.
A LAN describes a limited geographic network. It does not identify the private organisation-wide resource environment across the branch and headquarters.

sourceExplanation.text: Intranet is a term used to refer to a private connection of LANs and WANs that belongs to an organization. An intranet is designed to be accessible only by the organization's members, employees, or others with authorization.

questions.prompt: Which statement describes the use of powerline networking technology?

options.text: New “smart” electrical cabling is used to extend an existing home LAN.
A home LAN is installed without the use of physical cabling.
A device connects to an existing home LAN using an adapter and an existing electrical outlet.
Wireless access points use powerline adapters to distribute data through the home LAN.

summary.text: Powerline networking carries data over existing electrical wiring using adapters.

concept.text: Powerline networking carries data over existing electrical wiring using adapters. It reuses a physical medium rather than eliminating cabling, and results depend on the electrical installation.

rationale.text: New special electrical cabling is not the defining requirement; existing wiring is reused.
Electrical wires remain the transmission medium, so this is not a cable-free LAN.
A powerline adapter at an existing outlet provides the described network connection.
Some products combine Wi-Fi and powerline, but wireless access points are not required. The general mechanism is communication between powerline adapters over wiring.

sourceExplanation.text: Powerline networking adds the ability to connect a device to the network using an adapter wherever there is an electrical outlet. The network uses existing electrical wiring to send data. It is not a replacement for physical cabling, but it can add functionality in places where wireless access points cannot be used or cannot reach devices.

questions.prompt: A networking technician is working on the wireless network at a medical clinic. The technician accidentally sets up the wireless network so that patients can see the medical records data of other patients. Which of the four network characteristics has been violated in this situation?

summary.text: The exposed records violate confidentiality, a security objective.

concept.text: The exposed records violate confidentiality, a security objective. Availability, capacity growth and traffic prioritisation are different concerns.

rationale.text: Fault tolerance concerns continuing operation through component failures; the problem here is unauthorised disclosure.
Scalability concerns supporting growth without unacceptable degradation.
Security includes ensuring that only authorised users can read sensitive information; patients seeing other patients' records violates that requirement.
QoS prioritises traffic and manages delay or loss. It does not decide who may read a record.
Reliability concerns dependable operation. The specifically identified failure is confidentiality, not an outage.

sourceExplanation.text: Network security includes protecting the confidentiality of data that is on the network. In this case, because confidential data has been made available to unauthorized users, the security characteristic of the network has failed.

questions.prompt: Match each characteristic to its corresponding Internet connectivity type. (Not all options are used.)

prompts.text: DSL
dialup telephone
satellite
cable

choices.text: not suited for heavily wooded areas
high bandwidth connection that runs over telephone line
uses coaxial cable as a medium
typically uses a T1/E1 or T3/E3 circuit

summary.text: Associate the access technology with its physical medium and limitations.

concept.text: Associate the access technology with its physical medium and limitations. The leased-line statement is an unused distractor, not a match for dialup.

rationale.text: DSL carries broadband data over telephone-line copper. Dedicated T1/E1 or T3/E3 leased circuits are a different access service.
Dialup telephone uses a voice-band modem and has very low throughput compared with broadband. It is distinct from DSL even though both can use telephone wiring.
Satellite links need a suitable clear view toward the satellite; dense trees can obstruct the signal. The source is describing conventional home satellite access.
The cable option refers to broadband access using coaxial cable in the customer access segment. It is not the telephone-line DSL option.

sourceExplanation.text: DSL is an always-on, high bandwidth connection that runs over telephone lines. Cable uses the same coaxial cable that carries television signals into the home to provide Internet access. Dialup telephone is much slower than either DSL or cable, but is the least expensive option for home users because it can use any telephone line and a simple modem. Satellite requires a clear line of sight and is affected by trees and other obstructions. None of these typical home options use dedicated leased lines such as T1/E1 and T3/E3.

questions.prompt: What two criteria are used to help select a network medium from various network media? (Choose two.)

options.text: the types of data that need to be prioritized
the cost of the end devices utilized in the network
the distance the selected medium can successfully carry a signal
the number of intermediate devices installed in the network
the environment where the selected medium is to be installed

summary.text: Media selection must consider supported distance and installation conditions, as well as capacity and installation cost.

concept.text: Media selection must consider supported distance and installation conditions, as well as capacity and installation cost. A medium suitable for a short protected office run may be unsuitable over long distances or in electrical interference.

rationale.text: Traffic prioritisation is primarily a QoS policy decision; it is not one of the two direct physical-media criteria offered.
End-device price differs from the cost of the medium and its installation.
A medium must carry the signal across the required distance without exceeding its supported limits.
Device count alone does not establish whether the medium suits the link; link distance and surroundings directly constrain it.
Interference, moisture, physical exposure and similar environmental conditions affect the appropriate medium.

sourceExplanation.text: Criteria for choosing a network medium are the distance the selected medium can successfully carry a signal, the environment in which the selected medium is to be installed, the amount of data and the speed at which the data must be transmitted, and the cost of the medium and its installation.

questions.prompt: What type of network traffic requires QoS?

summary.text: Interactive video is sensitive to delay, jitter and loss.

concept.text: Interactive video is sensitive to delay, jitter and loss. QoS can prioritise it during contention, but cannot guarantee uninterrupted service or manufacture bandwidth.

rationale.text: Email generally tolerates delay and is less time-sensitive than a live conversation.
Purchasing transactions need reliability and security, but are generally less sensitive to steady real-time delivery than conferencing.
Live audio and video become difficult to use when packets arrive late or irregularly, making conferencing the best choice.
A wiki is ordinarily an asynchronous web application; short transfer delays do not disrupt a live conversation.

commonMistakes.text: QoS cannot guarantee uninterrupted video when capacity or connectivity is insufficient.

sourceExplanation.text: Video conferencing utilizes real-time audio and video communications. Both of these are time-sensitive and bandwidth-intensive forms of communication that require quality of service to be active on the network. QoS will ensure an uninterrupted user experience.

questions.prompt: A user is implementing security on a small office network. Which two actions would provide the minimum security requirements for this network? (Choose two.)

options.text: adding a dedicated intrusion prevention device

summary.text: The supplied introductory key pairs a firewall with antivirus for a small-office baseline.

concept.text: The supplied introductory key pairs a firewall with antivirus for a small-office baseline. This is a course simplification, not a complete modern security checklist: updates, authentication, backups and secure configuration also matter.

rationale.text: A firewall controls permitted network traffic and reduces exposure.
Adding Wi-Fi creates a connectivity option and potential attack surface; it is not itself a security control.
Antivirus or endpoint antimalware helps detect and stop malicious software.
An IDS detects suspicious activity and can be useful, but is not one of the two basic controls requested by this key.
An IPS can block suspicious traffic, but a dedicated appliance is beyond the two baseline controls selected here.

sourceExplanation.text: Technically complex security measures such as intrusion prevention and intrusion prevention systems are usually associated with business networks rather than home networks. Installing antivirus software, antimalware software, and implementing a firewall will usually be the minimum requirements for home networks. Installing a home wireless network will not improve network security, and will require further security actions to be taken.

questions.prompt: Passwords can be used to restrict access to all or parts of the Cisco IOS. Select the modes and interfaces that can be protected with passwords. (Choose three.)

summary.text: Classic IOS separates console access, remote terminal lines and privileged EXEC access.

concept.text: Classic IOS separates console access, remote terminal lines and privileged EXEC access. The wording calls VTY an interface, but VTYs are logical terminal lines.

rationale.text: VTY lines handle remote terminal access and can require authentication.
Console-line configuration can require a password for local terminal access.
An Ethernet port is not protected using the same line-password mechanism; features such as 802.1X are separate mechanisms.
Boot IOS mode is not one of the normal line or EXEC password targets in this question.
An enable secret can restrict escalation to privileged EXEC mode.
Global configuration is normally reached through privileged EXEC; this is not a separate basic line-password target.

sourceExplanation.text: Access to the VTY and console interfaces can be restricted using passwords. Out-of-band management of the router can be restricted in both user EXEC and privileged EXEC modes.

questions.prompt: Which interface allows remote management of a Layer 2 switch?

summary.text: A Layer 2 switch can use an IP address on an SVI for in-band management.

concept.text: A Layer 2 switch can use an IP address on an SVI for in-band management. Forwarding Ethernet frames does not itself require that management address.

rationale.text: An AUX connection is not the standard IP management interface of the Layer 2 switch described.
The console provides direct terminal access rather than the requested in-band network management interface.
The SVI is a logical VLAN interface to which the management IP address can be assigned.
An ordinary Layer 2 Ethernet switchport carries frames; the management IP belongs on the SVI in this scenario.

sourceExplanation.text: In a Layer 2 switch, there is a switch virtual interface (SVI) that provides a means for remotely managing the device.

questions.prompt: What function does pressing the Tab key have when entering a command in IOS?

options.text: It aborts the current command and returns to configuration mode.
It exits configuration mode and returns to user EXEC mode.
It moves the cursor to the beginning of the next line.
It completes the remainder of a partially typed word in a command.

summary.text: Tab completes an unambiguous IOS keyword.

concept.text: Tab completes an unambiguous IOS keyword. If several keywords match the prefix, more characters are needed before completion is possible.

rationale.text: Tab does not abort the current operation.
Tab does not navigate out of configuration mode.
Tab is completion, not a command to move to the next line.
IOS expands a sufficiently specific partially typed keyword when Tab is pressed.

sourceExplanation.text: Pressing the Tab key after a command has been partially typed will cause the IOS to complete the rest of the command.

questions.prompt: While trying to solve a network issue, a technician made multiple changes to the current router configuration file. The changes did not solve the problem and were not saved. What action can the technician take to discard the changes and work with the file in NVRAM?

options.text: Issue the reload command without saving the running configuration.
Delete the vlan.dat file and reboot the device.
Close and reopen the terminal emulation software.
Issue the copy startup-config running-config command.

summary.text: On the classic IOS model, reloading without saving discards unsaved running-config changes and loads startup-config from NVRAM.

concept.text: On the classic IOS model, reloading without saving discards unsaved running-config changes and loads startup-config from NVRAM. This interrupts service; use it deliberately in a lab or maintenance window.

rationale.text: This reload uses the saved startup configuration instead of retaining the failed unsaved edits.
vlan.dat concerns VLAN information and is not a general rollback for router configuration edits.
Closing the terminal session does not undo changes already applied to the device.
Copying startup-config into running-config generally merges configuration. It need not remove extra commands introduced during troubleshooting.

commonMistakes.text: copy startup-config running-config merges; it is not a reliable general undo.

sourceExplanation.text: The technician does not want to make any mistakes trying to remove all the changes that were done to the running configuration file. The solution is to reboot the router without saving the running configuration. The copy startup-config running-config command does not overwrite the running configuration file with the configuration file stored in NVRAM, but rather it just has an additive effect.

questions.prompt: An administrator uses the Ctrl-Shift-6 key combination on a switch after issuing the ping command. What is the purpose of using these keystrokes?

options.text: to exit to a different configuration mode
to allow the user to complete the command

summary.text: Ctrl-Shift-6 is the IOS escape sequence used to interrupt operations such as ping.

concept.text: Ctrl-Shift-6 is the IOS escape sequence used to interrupt operations such as ping. Distinguish interrupting an operation from command completion or changing configuration modes.

rationale.text: It stops the current operation rather than starting a new ping.
This is the intended interruption mechanism for the running ping.
It is not the command-hierarchy navigation action being asked about.
Tab provides completion; Ctrl-Shift-6 interrupts a running operation.

sourceExplanation.text: To interrupt an IOS process such as ping or traceroute, a user enters the Ctrl-Shift-6 key combination. Tab completes the remainder of parameters or arguments within a command. To exit from configuration mode to privileged mode use the Ctrl-Z keystroke. CTRL-R will redisplay the line just typed, thus making it easier for the user to press Enter and reissue the ping command.

questions.prompt: Refer to the exhibit. A network administrator is configuring access control to switch SW1. If the administrator uses a console connection to connect to the switch, which password is needed to access user EXEC mode?

summary.text: The console login password is selected by the line console 0 configuration.

concept.text: The console login password is selected by the line console 0 configuration. Enable credentials control later escalation to privileged EXEC, while VTY credentials apply to remote lines.

rationale.text: letmein is configured with enable password, so it concerns privileged access rather than initial console login.
secretin is the enable secret, used for privileged EXEC access rather than user EXEC console login.
lineconin is the password under line console 0 with login enabled.
linevtyin is configured for VTY lines, not the console line used in this question.

sourceExplanation.text: Telnet accesses a network device through the virtual interface configured with the line VTY command. The password configured under this is required to access the user EXEC mode. The password configured under the line console 0 command is required to gain entry through the console port, and the enable and enable secret passwords are used to allow entry into the privileged EXEC mode.

questions.prompt: A technician configures a switch with these commands: What is the technician configuring?

blocks.text:
SwitchA(config)# interface vlan 1
SwitchA(config-if)# ip address 192.168.1.1 255.255.255.0
SwitchA(config-if)# no shutdown

summary.text: interface vlan 1 selects an SVI; ip address assigns its IPv4 address and no shutdown removes its administrative shutdown.

concept.text: interface vlan 1 selects an SVI; ip address assigns its IPv4 address and no shutdown removes its administrative shutdown. Operational status still depends on the VLAN and relevant active ports.

rationale.text: These commands do not configure VTY authentication or enable a Telnet service by themselves.
The selected interface is VLAN 1, a switch virtual interface used here for management.
No password-encryption command appears.
A physical port would be selected with a hardware interface name such as GigabitEthernet; interface vlan selects a logical interface.

intro.text: In a lab switch, configure the logical VLAN interface, then verify its state separately.

practicalExample.code:
interface vlan 1
 ip address 192.168.1.1 255.255.255.0
 no shutdown

sourceExplanation.text: For a switch to have an IP address, a switch virtual interface must be configured. This allows the switch to be managed remotely over the network.

questions.prompt: Which command or key combination allows a user to return to the previous level in the command hierarchy?

summary.text: exit leaves the current configuration submode for its parent.

concept.text: exit leaves the current configuration submode for its parent. end and Ctrl-Z normally return directly to privileged EXEC instead of moving only one configuration level.

rationale.text: end skips back to privileged EXEC, potentially crossing multiple configuration levels.
exit is the ordinary one-level navigation command within the configuration hierarchy.
Ctrl-Z normally returns directly to privileged EXEC.
Ctrl-C cancels input or an operation and may leave configuration mode; it is not the general one-level navigation command.

sourceExplanation.text: End and CTRL-Z return the user to the privileged EXEC mode. Ctrl-C ends a command in process. The exit command returns the user to the previous level.

questions.prompt: What are two characteristics of RAM on a Cisco device? (Choose two.)

options.text: The configuration that is actively running on the device is stored in RAM.
The contents of RAM are lost during a power cycle.
RAM is a component in Cisco switches but not in Cisco routers.
RAM is able to store multiple versions of IOS and configuration files.

summary.text: RAM is volatile working memory used by both routers and switches.

concept.text: RAM is volatile working memory used by both routers and switches. In the introductory IOS model it holds running-config; startup-config is retained separately in nonvolatile storage.

rationale.text: RAM is volatile, so this reverses its defining property.
The active running configuration is held in RAM in the model tested here.
Removing power loses volatile RAM contents.
Routers also use RAM; it is not exclusive to switches.
Persistent storage of multiple IOS images and saved files is associated with flash. RAM can hold working data but is not the intended durable repository.

sourceExplanation.text: RAM stores data that is used by the device to support network operations. The running configuration is stored in RAM. This type of memory is considered volatile memory because data is lost during a power cycle. Flash memory stores the IOS and delivers a copy of the IOS into RAM when a device is powered on. Flash memory is nonvolatile since it retains stored contents during a loss of power.

questions.prompt: Which two host names follow the guidelines for naming conventions on Cisco IOS devices? (Choose two.)

summary.text: Use an IOS hostname beginning with a letter, ending in a letter or digit, and containing letters, digits or hyphens without spaces.

concept.text: Use an IOS hostname beginning with a letter, ending in a letter or digit, and containing letters, digits or hyphens without spaces. Both selected names satisfy these course naming rules.

rationale.text: The exclamation mark violates the allowed-character guideline.
This begins with a letter, uses permitted hyphens and digits, and ends with a digit.
Parentheses violate the allowed-character guideline.
Spaces are not permitted under the naming convention.
This uses letters and digits, starts with a letter and ends with a digit.

sourceExplanation.text: Some guidelines for naming conventions are that names should: Start with a letter Contain no spaces End with a letter or digit Use only letters, digits, and dashes Be less than 64 characters in length

questions.prompt: How is SSH different from Telnet?

options.text: SSH makes connections over the network, whereas Telnet is for out-of-band access.
SSH provides security to remote sessions by encrypting messages and using user authentication. Telnet is considered insecure and sends messages in plaintext.
SSH requires the use of the PuTTY terminal emulation program. Tera Term must be used to connect to devices through the use of Telnet.
SSH must be configured over an active network connection, whereas Telnet is used to connect to a device from a console connection.

summary.text: SSH protects a remote terminal session through encryption and authentication; ordinary Telnet sends session content in cleartext.

concept.text: SSH protects a remote terminal session through encryption and authentication; ordinary Telnet sends session content in cleartext. Both are network-based management protocols.

rationale.text: Telnet also operates over the network, so the claimed in-band/out-of-band distinction is false.
This identifies the relevant protection difference. Telnet may also ask for a login, but its ordinary transport does not protect the exchanged data.
Client choice is not exclusive: terminal applications may support both protocols.
Either service can be configured via a console; using Telnet itself requires network connectivity.

commonMistakes.text: Telnet can authenticate a user and still expose that login in plaintext.

sourceExplanation.text: SSH is the preferred protocol for connecting to a device operating system over the network because it is much more secure than Telnet. Both SSH and Telnet are used to connect to devices over the network, and so are both used in-band. PuTTY and Terra Term can be used to make both SSH and Telnet connections.

questions.prompt: An administrator is configuring a switch console port with a password. In what order will the administrator travel through the IOS modes of operation in order to reach the mode in which the configuration commands will be entered? (Not all options are used.)

summary.text: The sequence is user EXEC → privileged EXEC → global configuration → line configuration.

concept.text: The sequence is user EXEC → privileged EXEC → global configuration → line configuration. Enter enable, configure terminal, then line console 0. Interface configuration is a genuine distractor in the test PDF and is retained.

rationale.text: Unused: physical interface configuration is not where the console-line password is set.
Second: enable moves from user EXEC to privileged EXEC, which allows entry to configuration.
Fourth: line console 0 selects the console line so its password and login settings can be configured.
Third: configure terminal enters global configuration, from which the line console 0 submode is selected.
First: user EXEC is the starting mode assumed in this basic exercise.

sourceExplanation.text: The configuration mode that the administrator first encounters is user EXEC mode. After the enable command is entered, the next mode is privileged EXEC mode. From there, the configure terminal command is entered to move to global configuration mode. Finally, the administrator enters the line console 0 command to enter the mode in which the configuration will be entered.

editorialNotes.reason: Equivalent order interaction retains the interface-configuration distractor visible in the test PDF.

questions.prompt: What are three characteristics of an SVI? (Choose three.)

options.text: It is designed as a security protocol to protect switch ports.
It is not associated with any physical interface on a switch.
It is a special interface that allows connectivity by different types of media.
It is required to allow connectivity by any device at any location.
It provides a means to remotely manage a switch.
It is associated with VLAN1 by default.

summary.text: An SVI is a software interface associated with a VLAN.

concept.text: An SVI is a software interface associated with a VLAN. In the introductory default-switch scenario VLAN 1 has an SVI; additional SVIs may be configured for other VLANs. It is not a physical connector.

rationale.text: An SVI is an interface, not a port-security protocol.
It has no dedicated physical connector. Its operational status may still depend on active ports in its VLAN.
Supporting different physical media is a hardware/transceiver matter, not the defining SVI function.
Devices can communicate at Layer 2 without a management SVI; universal connectivity is not guaranteed by it.
An IP address on an SVI can make the switch reachable for remote management.
The default VLAN 1 SVI is the course scenario. This does not mean every SVI must belong to VLAN 1.

commonMistakes.text: An SVI is tied to a VLAN, not a dedicated physical socket.

sourceExplanation.text: Switches have one or more switch virtual interfaces (SVIs). SVIs are created in software since there is no physical hardware associated with them. Virtual interfaces provide a means to remotely manage a switch over a network that is using IP. Each switch comes with one SVI appearing in the default configuration "out-of-the-box." The default SVI interface is VLAN1.

questions.prompt: What command is used to verify the condition of the switch interfaces, including the status of the interfaces and a configured IP address?

summary.text: show ip interface brief summarises interface IP addresses and administrative/line-protocol status.

concept.text: show ip interface brief summarises interface IP addresses and administrative/line-protocol status. Read both Status and Protocol: an address alone does not prove that an interface is usable.

rationale.text: ipconfig is a host-side command, not the IOS summary command requested.
ping tests reachability; it does not list all interfaces and their configured addresses.
traceroute investigates the routed path, not the local interface inventory.
This command displays the concise address-and-status summary requested.

intro.text: Check the IP-Address, Status and Protocol columns; administratively down differs from a physical or VLAN dependency.

sourceExplanation.text: The show ip interface brief command is used to display a brief synopsis of the condition of the device interfaces. The ipconfig command is used to verify TCP/IP properties on a host. The ping command is used to verify Layer 3 connectivity. The traceroute command is used to trace the network path from source to destination.

questions.prompt: Match the description with the associated IOS mode. (Not all options are used.)

prompts.text: changes made affect the operation of the device as a whole
accessed by entering the enable command
identified by a prompt ending with the # character
limited number of basic monitoring commands
accessed by entering the configure terminal command
the first entrance into the CLI of an IOS device
used to enable the password for vty lines

summary.text: Match each description to an IOS mode.

concept.text: Match each description to an IOS mode. Categories may be used more than once; choose Not used for the VTY-line configuration statement.

rationale.text: Global configuration changes device-wide settings. Interface or line-specific settings belong to narrower submodes.
From user EXEC, enable requests privileged EXEC access and may require authentication.
The intended prompt is Device# for privileged EXEC. Configuration prompts also end in #, so inspect the entire prompt, including any parenthesised mode.
User EXEC offers a limited set of basic commands before elevation.
From privileged EXEC, configure terminal enters global configuration.
In the basic default-login scenario, the first mode is user EXEC. AAA or configured privilege levels can change that real-world behaviour.
This is unused because VTY password/login settings are entered in line configuration mode, which is not one of the three offered categories.

editorialNotes.originalText: Descriptions dragged into three mode groups
editorialNotes.revisedText: Seven description prompts with reusable mode choices and explicit Not used
editorialNotes.reason: Preserves many-to-one grouping and the unused VTY item without publishing the answered screenshot.

questions.prompt: Match the definitions to their respective CLI hot keys and shortcuts. (Not all options are used.)

prompts.text: displays the next screen
scrolls backwards through previously entered commands
provides context-sensitive help
completes abbreviated commands and parameters
aborts commands such as trace and ping

summary.text: CLI shortcuts perform different jobs: pagination, history, help, completion and interruption.

concept.text: CLI shortcuts perform different jobs: pagination, history, help, completion and interruption. The same key may behave differently depending on the terminal context.

rationale.text: Space advances one screen at a paginated --More-- prompt; Enter advances a line.
Up Arrow recalls earlier commands from history; it does not invoke context help.
The question-mark key requests context-sensitive help at the current command position.
Tab completes an unambiguous command or keyword prefix. It cannot choose between multiple valid completions without more input.
Ctrl-Shift-6 interrupts an IOS process such as ping or traceroute. Ctrl-C is the unused input-cancellation distractor in this exercise.

sourceExplanation.text: The shortcuts with their functions are as follows: - Tab - Completes the remainder of a partially typed command or keyword - Space bar - displays the next screen - ? - provides context-sensitive help - Up Arrow - Allows user to scroll backward through former commands - Ctrl-C - cancels any command currently being entered and returns directly to privileged EXEC mode - Ctrl-Shift-6 - Allows the user to interrupt an IOS process such as ping or traceroute

questions.prompt: In the show running-config command, which part of the syntax is represented by running-config?

summary.text: In show running-config, show is the command and running-config is a fixed keyword selecting the information to display.

concept.text: In show running-config, show is the command and running-config is a fixed keyword selecting the information to display. An argument such as a chosen IP address would be variable input.

rationale.text: The primary command is show; the question asks about the following token.
running-config is the fixed keyword choosing the active configuration output.
It is a predefined token rather than a user-selected value.
The prompt is the device/mode indicator, such as Switch#, before the command.

sourceExplanation.text: The first part of the syntax, show, is the command, and the second part of the syntax, running-config, is the keyword. The keyword specifies what should be displayed as the output of the show command.

questions.prompt: After making configuration changes on a Cisco switch, a network administrator issues a copy running-config startup-config command. What is the result of issuing this command?

options.text: The new configuration will be stored in flash memory.
The new configuration will be loaded if the switch is restarted.
The current IOS file will be replaced with the newly configured file.
The configuration changes will be removed and the original configuration will be restored.

summary.text: copy running-config startup-config saves the active configuration for later startup.

concept.text: copy running-config startup-config saves the active configuration for later startup. It does not save a new operating-system image or reverse the edits.

rationale.text: The classic course model places startup-config in NVRAM. Platform storage details can vary, but persistence on restart is the intended result.
A normal subsequent restart loads the saved configuration, assuming it is not bypassed or changed.
An IOS image is distinct from configuration commands; this does not replace the image.
The command preserves current edits rather than reverting them.

intro.text: After validating a lab configuration, save the active settings for the next normal startup.

sourceExplanation.text: With the copy running-config startup-config command, the content of the current operating configuration replaces the startup configuration file stored in NVRAM. The configuration file saved in NVRAM will be loaded when the device is restarted.

questions.prompt: What command will prevent all unencrypted passwords from displaying in plain text in a configuration file?

summary.text: In the classic IOS context, service password-encryption hides supported cleartext configuration passwords using reversible type 7 obfuscation.

concept.text: In the classic IOS context, service password-encryption hides supported cleartext configuration passwords using reversible type 7 obfuscation. It is not strong secret protection and does not encrypt network traffic.

rationale.text: This configures an enable password whose literal value is secret; it does not cover other passwords.
This sets one enable secret rather than obscuring all eligible line passwords.
This sets a line password with the value secret; it is not a global encryption setting.
This is the intended global command for obscuring supported cleartext password fields in the legacy configuration.
The text Encrypted_Password is merely the supplied value; the command still concerns only the enable secret.

commonMistakes.text: Obscuring a password is not the same as securely protecting a secret.

sourceExplanation.text: To prevent all configured passwords from appearing in plain text in configuration files, an administrator can execute the service password-encryption command. This command encrypts all configured passwords in the configuration file.

questions.prompt: A network administrator enters the service password-encryption command into the configuration mode of a router. What does this command accomplish?

options.text: This command encrypts passwords as they are transmitted across serial WAN links.
This command prevents someone from viewing the running configuration passwords.
This command enables a strong encryption algorithm for the enable secret password command.
This command automatically encrypts passwords in configuration files that are currently stored in NVRAM.
This command provides an exclusive encrypted password for external service personnel who are required to do router maintenance.

summary.text: The supplied key means preventing casual reading of plaintext password values in the configuration.

concept.text: The supplied key means preventing casual reading of plaintext password values in the configuration. Legacy type 7 values remain visible and reversible, so the command does not prevent determined recovery.

rationale.text: It changes stored configuration representation, not encryption of packets on a WAN link.
This is the intended answer only in the limited sense of obscuring cleartext values; access to the configuration still exposes recoverable type 7 strings.
The enable secret mechanism is separate; this does not upgrade its hashing algorithm.
Do not assume previously saved startup-config is rewritten automatically. Save the changed running configuration to persist it.
It neither creates a special maintenance account nor assigns a separate service-personnel password.

commonMistakes.text: A type 7 string can be recovered; protect configuration files.

sourceExplanation.text: The startup-config and running-config files display most passwords in plaintext. Use the service password-encryption global config command to encrypt all plaintext passwords in these files.

questions.prompt: What method can be used by two computers to ensure that packets are not dropped because too much data is being sent too quickly?

summary.text: Flow control limits a sender so it does not overwhelm the receiver.

concept.text: Flow control limits a sender so it does not overwhelm the receiver. It addresses receiver capacity; it does not promise that packets can never be lost elsewhere in a network.

rationale.text: Encapsulation adds protocol structure around data; it does not itself regulate the sender's rate.
Flow control coordinates how much data may be sent relative to what the receiver can accept.
An access method determines use of a shared medium, not primarily receiver buffer capacity.
A timeout detects a delayed or missing response; it does not directly pace the incoming data stream.

sourceExplanation.text: In order for two computers to be able to communicate effectively, there must be a mechanism that allows both the source and destination to set the timing of the transmission and receipt of data. Flow control allows for this by ensuring that data is not sent too fast for it to be received properly.

questions.prompt: Which statement accurately describes a TCP/IP encapsulation process when a PC is sending data to the network?

options.text: Data is sent from the internet layer to the network access layer.
Packets are sent from the network access layer to the transport layer.
Segments are sent from the transport layer to the internet layer.
Frames are sent from the network access layer to the internet layer.

summary.text: For sending, TCP segments pass from transport to the Internet layer, where IP encapsulates them into packets.

concept.text: For sending, TCP segments pass from transport to the Internet layer, where IP encapsulates them into packets. The source's generic word data makes the first distractor imprecise; the intended key uses the specific PDU name and adjacent layers.

rationale.text: Broadly data does move downward, but the specific PDU leaving the Internet layer is a packet. This wording is ambiguous, so retain an editorial warning rather than teaching that no data crosses these layers.
This skips the Internet layer and describes upward rather than outbound encapsulation.
A transport segment becomes the payload of an Internet-layer packet, matching the sending direction.
Frames are formed at network access for transmission. Sending them upward describes reception rather than this outbound process.

commonMistakes.text: PDU names matter, but vague source wording must not be treated as a technical impossibility.

sourceExplanation.text: When the data is traveling from the PC to the network, the transport layer sends segments to the internet layer. The internet layer sends packets to the network access layer, which creates frames and then converts the frames to bits. The bits are released to the network media.

questions.prompt: What three application layer protocols are part of the TCP/IP protocol suite? (Choose three.)

summary.text: DHCP, DNS and FTP provide application services.

concept.text: DHCP, DNS and FTP provide application services. ARP resolves local next-hop addressing, PPP handles a link, and NAT translates network addresses; NAT is a function rather than a standalone application protocol.

rationale.text: ARP resolves an IPv4 address to a link-layer address on the local link; it is not an application service here.
DHCP supplies host configuration through an application-layer exchange.
DNS resolves names and other resource records through an application-layer service.
FTP is an application-layer file-transfer protocol.
NAT translates addresses and sometimes ports; it is not an application-layer protocol.
PPP provides point-to-point link framing and control rather than an application service.

sourceExplanation.text: DNS, DHCP, and FTP are all application layer protocols in the TCP/IP protocol suite. ARP and PPP are network access layer protocols, and NAT is an internet layer protocol in the TCP/IP protocol suite.

questions.prompt: Match the description to the organization. (Not all options are used.)

prompts.text: This organization is responsible for overseeing and managing IP address allocation, domain name management, and protocol identifiers.
This organization is the largest developer of international standards in the world for a wide variety of products and services. It is known for its Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) reference model.
This organization promotes the open development, evolution, and use of the Internet throughout the world.

summary.text: Distinguish standards development, Internet advocacy and identifier coordination.

concept.text: Distinguish standards development, Internet advocacy and identifier coordination. The source diagram is partly obscured in the answer PDF, so this mapping uses the readable question text and the listed primary references.

rationale.text: IANA coordinates globally unique Internet identifiers, including IP/AS number spaces, the DNS root and protocol registries. It does not personally allocate every end-user address or register every domain.
ISO develops international standards; the OSI reference model is published as ISO/IEC 7498-1. This identifies ISO in the course options.
ISOC supports Internet development and open use. It is not the identifier-allocation function (IANA). EIA is an unused historical electronics-standards distractor.

sourceExplanation.text: The EIA is an international standards and trade organization for electronics organizations. It is best known for its standards related to electrical wiring, connectors, and the 19-inch racks used to mount networking equipment.

questions.prompt: Which name is assigned to the transport layer PDU?

summary.text: The course uses segment for the transport-layer PDU, particularly TCP.

concept.text: The course uses segment for the transport-layer PDU, particularly TCP. UDP uses datagram; do not infer that all transport protocols provide TCP's segmentation or reliability.

rationale.text: Bits are associated with physical transmission.
Data is the generic upper-layer label in this teaching model.
A frame is the data-link PDU.
A packet is the network-layer PDU in this model.
Segment is the intended transport PDU label, specifically appropriate to TCP.

commonMistakes.text: TCP segments and UDP datagrams are both transport-layer units.

sourceExplanation.text: Application data is passed down the protocol stack on its way to be transmitted across the network media. During the process, various protocols add information to it at each level. At each stage of the process, a PDU (protocol data unit) has a different name to reflect its new functions. The PDUs are named according to the protocols of the TCP/IP suite: Data - The general term for the PDU used at the application layer. Segment - transport layer PDU Packet - network layer PDU Frame – data link layer PDU Bits - A physical layer PDU used when physically transmitting data over the medium

questions.prompt: When IPv4 addressing is manually configured on a web server, which property of the IPv4 configuration identifies the network and host portion for an IPv4 address?

summary.text: The subnet mask identifies which IPv4 address bits are network bits and which are host bits.

concept.text: The subnet mask identifies which IPv4 address bits are network bits and which are host bits. For example, 255.255.255.0 is /24: 24 network bits and 8 host bits.

rationale.text: A DNS server resolves names; its address does not specify the local address boundary.
The mask supplies the bit boundary used to determine the subnet.
A default gateway identifies a next-hop router for destinations outside the local subnet.
A DHCP server can supply a mask automatically, but its own address is not the mask and is not what determines the bit boundary.

sourceExplanation.text: There are several components that need to be entered when configuring IPv4 for an end device: IPv4 address - uniquely identifies an end device on the network Subnet mask - determines the network address portion and host portion for an IPv4 address Default gateway - the IP address of the router interface used for communicating with hosts in another network DNS server address - the IP address of the Domain Name System (DNS) server DHCP server address (if DHCP is used) is not configured manually on end devices. It will be provided by a DHCP server when an end device requests an IP address.

questions.prompt: What process involves placing one PDU inside of another PDU?

summary.text: Encapsulation puts one protocol's PDU inside the payload of a lower-layer PDU.

concept.text: Encapsulation puts one protocol's PDU inside the payload of a lower-layer PDU. For example, a TCP segment is carried in an IP packet, which is carried in an Ethernet frame.

rationale.text: This is the nesting process described.
Encoding represents information as symbols or signals; it is not the PDU-nesting operation.
Segmentation divides a larger data stream into smaller units rather than wrapping one unit in another.
Flow control regulates delivery relative to receiving capacity; it does not describe nesting.

sourceExplanation.text: When a message is placed inside of another message, this is known as encapsulation. On networks, encapsulation takes place when one protocol data unit is carried inside of the data field of the next lower protocol data unit.

questions.prompt: What layer is responsible for routing messages through an internetwork in the TCP/IP model?

summary.text: The TCP/IP Internet layer provides IP addressing and routing across interconnected networks.

concept.text: The TCP/IP Internet layer provides IP addressing and routing across interconnected networks. In the OSI comparison this is the network-layer role.

rationale.text: This is the layer responsible for IP forwarding through an internetwork.
Transport addresses communication between applications, using mechanisms such as ports.
Network access handles local link delivery and physical transmission rather than internetwork routing.
Session is an OSI layer name, not a separate layer in the four-layer TCP/IP model.

sourceExplanation.text: The TCP/IP model consists of four layers: application, transport, internet, and network access. Of these four layers, it is the internet layer that is responsible for routing messages. The session layer is not part of the TCP/IP model but is rather part of the OSI model.

questions.prompt: For the TCP/IP protocol suite, what is the correct order of events when a Telnet message is being prepared to be sent over the network?

items.text: The Telnet-formatted data is provided to the next layer.

summary.text: Sending encapsulates from inner application data to outer link framing: Telnet data → TCP → IP → Ethernet.

concept.text: Sending encapsulates from inner application data to outer link framing: Telnet data → TCP → IP → Ethernet. Swapping TCP and IP would put headers at the wrong nesting levels.

rationale.text: Third: the IP header wraps the TCP segment to form an IP packet.
Second: TCP adds its transport header to the Telnet application data.
Fourth: Ethernet adds link framing around the IP packet. A complete Ethernet frame also has a trailer, even though the source item names only the header.
First: Telnet produces application data for TCP to carry. Telnet is the legacy example here; use SSH for protected remote administration.

questions.prompt: Which PDU format is used when bits are received from the network medium by the NIC of a host?

summary.text: The receiving NIC processes link-layer frames represented by the incoming bits.

concept.text: The receiving NIC processes link-layer frames represented by the incoming bits. The enclosed IP packet and transport data are interpreted higher in the stack.

rationale.text: A file may be application content, but is not the NIC's link-layer PDU.
A frame is the data-link structure reconstructed from received physical signals.
An IP packet is contained within the frame and is processed at the network layer.
A TCP segment is transport-layer content inside the packet.

sourceExplanation.text: When received at the physical layer of a host, the bits are formatted into a frame at the data link layer. A packet is the PDU at the network layer. A segment is the PDU at the transport layer. A file is a data structure that may be used at the application layer.

questions.prompt: Refer to the exhibit. ServerB is attempting to contact HostA. Which two statements correctly identify the addressing that ServerB will generate in the process? (Choose two.)

options.text: ServerB will generate a packet with the destination IP address of RouterB.
ServerB will generate a frame with the destination MAC address of SwitchB.
ServerB will generate a packet with the destination IP address of RouterA.
ServerB will generate a frame with the destination MAC address of RouterB.
ServerB will generate a packet with the destination IP address of HostA.
ServerB will generate a frame with the destination MAC address of RouterA.

summary.text: ServerB sends an IP packet addressed to the final remote host, but its first Ethernet frame is addressed to the local default gateway.

concept.text: ServerB sends an IP packet addressed to the final remote host, but its first Ethernet frame is addressed to the local default gateway. Without NAT, the endpoint IP addresses persist across routers while link-layer headers change at each hop.

rationale.text: RouterB is the next hop, not the final IP recipient of the communication to HostA.
SwitchB forwards the frame, but ordinary transit traffic is not addressed to the switch's own management MAC.
RouterA is an intermediate router, not the final host IP destination.
RouterB's local interface is ServerB's default gateway, so its MAC is the first-hop destination.
HostA remains the final IP destination even though it is on a remote network.
RouterA is not directly on ServerB's local Ethernet link; ServerB first addresses RouterB's local interface.

commonMistakes.text: A local switch is not normally the destination MAC for transit frames.

sourceExplanation.text: In order to send data to HostA, ServerB will generate a packet that contains the IP address of the destination device on the remote network and a frame that contains the MAC address of the default gateway device on the local network.

questions.prompt: Which method allows a computer to react accordingly when it requests data from a server and the server takes too long to respond?

summary.text: A response timeout defines how long to wait before treating a reply as overdue.

concept.text: A response timeout defines how long to wait before treating a reply as overdue. The application or protocol may then retry, report failure or take another action.

rationale.text: Encapsulation structures data but does not set a waiting limit.
Flow control paces a sender relative to receiver capacity; it is not a response deadline.
An access method governs medium access rather than how long to wait for a server reply.
A response timeout lets the requester react when the expected reply has not arrived within the allowed interval.

sourceExplanation.text: If a computer makes a request and does not hear a response within an acceptable amount of time, the computer assumes that no answer is coming and reacts accordingly.

questions.prompt: A web client is receiving a response for a web page from a web server. From the perspective of the client, what is the correct order of the protocol stack that is used to decode the received transmission?

summary.text: For the HTTP-over-TCP-over-IP-over-Ethernet scenario, reception proceeds from outer framing to inner application data: Ethernet, IP, TCP, HTTP.

concept.text: For the HTTP-over-TCP-over-IP-over-Ethernet scenario, reception proceeds from outer framing to inner application data: Ethernet, IP, TCP, HTTP. This reverses sending encapsulation; it is not a claim about every version of HTTP.

rationale.text: This follows the received nesting from link layer through network and transport to application.
This is the outbound encapsulation direction, not the receiving order.
IP must be interpreted before the TCP payload inside it; the middle layers are reversed.
HTTP cannot be decoded first from an unprocessed Ethernet frame, and the remaining sequence is also misplaced.

sourceExplanation.text: 1. HTTP governs the way that a web server and client interact. 2. TCP manages individual conversations between web servers and clients. 3. IP is responsible for delivery across the best path to the destination. 4. Ethernet takes the packet from IP and formats it for transmission.

questions.prompt: Which two OSI model layers have the same functionality as a single layer of the TCP/IP model? (Choose two.)

summary.text: In the four-layer TCP/IP model, network access combines OSI physical and data-link functions.

concept.text: In the four-layer TCP/IP model, network access combines OSI physical and data-link functions. OSI application, presentation and session map collectively to TCP/IP application.

rationale.text: Data link contributes framing and local delivery to network access.
OSI network corresponds to TCP/IP Internet, rather than the two-layer network-access grouping asked for.
Physical contributes signalling and media transmission to network access.
Session maps into TCP/IP application with two other OSI layers; it is not one of the requested network-access pair.
Transport has a corresponding transport layer in both models, rather than being part of the requested pair.

sourceExplanation.text: The OSI data link and physical layers together are equivalent to the TCP/IP network access layer. The OSI transport layer is functionally equivalent to the TCP/IP transport layer, and the OSI network layer is equivalent to the TCP/IP internet layer. The OSI application, presentation, and session layers are functionally equivalent to the application layer within the TCP/IP model.

questions.prompt: At which layer of the OSI model would a logical address be added during encapsulation?

summary.text: IP source and destination addresses are logical network-layer addresses.

concept.text: IP source and destination addresses are logical network-layer addresses. MAC addresses apply to a local link and TCP/UDP ports identify transport endpoints.

rationale.text: Physical signalling does not add an IP address.
Data link adds link-layer addressing such as Ethernet MAC addresses.
The network layer adds the IP addressing used for internetwork delivery.
Transport adds information such as source and destination ports, not the IP addresses.

sourceExplanation.text: Logical addresses, also known as IP addresses, are added at the network layer. Physical addresses are edded at the data link layer. Port addresses are added at the transport layer. No addresses are added at the physical layer.

questions.prompt: What is a characteristic of multicast messages?

options.text: They are sent to a select group of hosts.
They are sent to all hosts on a network.
They are sent to a single destination.

summary.text: Multicast addresses a group of receivers interested in particular traffic.

concept.text: Multicast addresses a group of receivers interested in particular traffic. It differs from unicast to one endpoint and broadcast to all devices in the relevant broadcast domain.

rationale.text: A selected multicast group is the defining recipient set.
Sending to all hosts in a broadcast domain describes broadcast, not multicast.
Multicast does not inherently require an acknowledgement from every receiver.
A single individual destination describes unicast; a multicast group address represents group membership.

sourceExplanation.text: Multicast is a one-to-many type of communication. Multicast messages are addressed to a specific multicast group.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about network protocols?

options.text: Network protocols define the type of hardware that is used and how it is mounted in racks.
They define how messages are exchanged between the source and the destination.
They all function in the network access layer of TCP/IP.
They are only required for exchange of messages between devices on remote networks.

summary.text: Protocols specify agreed communication rules, including message structure, meaning, sequencing and timing.

concept.text: Protocols specify agreed communication rules, including message structure, meaning, sequencing and timing. They operate across layers and are needed on local as well as remote networks.

rationale.text: Physical mounting standards are not the general purpose of network communication protocols.
Rules for exchanging messages are the defining function of a protocol.
Protocols also operate at Internet, transport and application layers.
Local communication also requires agreed protocols; crossing a router is not a prerequisite.

sourceExplanation.text: Network protocols are implemented in hardware, or software, or both. They interact with each other within different layers of a protocol stack. Protocols have nothing to do with the installation of the network equipment. Network protocols are required to exchange information between source and destination devices in both local and remote networks.

questions.prompt: What is an advantage of network devices using open standard protocols?

options.text: Network communications is confined to data transfers between devices from the same vendor.
A client host and a server running different operating systems can successfully exchange data.
Internet access can be controlled by a single ISP in each market.
Competition and innovation are limited to specific types of products.

summary.text: Open protocol standards let independently developed systems interoperate when they implement the same specifications.

concept.text: Open protocol standards let independently developed systems interoperate when they implement the same specifications. They reduce dependence on a single vendor but do not guarantee every implementation is compatible.

rationale.text: Confinement to a single vendor is the opposite of the interoperability benefit.
Different operating systems can communicate using a shared protocol specification.
A single-provider monopoly is not an advantage established by open protocols.
Shared standards can support broader competition and innovation rather than restrict them to particular products.

sourceExplanation.text: An advantage of network devices implementing open standard protocols, such as from the TCP/IP suite, is that clients and servers running different operating systems can communicate with each other. Open standard protocols facilitate innovation and competition between vendors and across markets, and can reduce the occurrence of monopolies in networking markets.

questions.prompt: Which device performs the function of determining the path that messages should take through internetworks?

summary.text: Routing chooses a next hop toward a destination network using routing information.

concept.text: Routing chooses a next hop toward a destination network using routing information. Products may combine several functions, but router is the device role named by this task.

rationale.text: Selecting paths between networks is the defining router function.
A firewall primarily enforces traffic policy; some firewalls also route, but that is not the role being distinguished here.
A web server provides application content rather than determining general forwarding paths.
A DSL modem terminates a subscriber access technology; an integrated modem-router may also route, but modem is not the path-selection role.

sourceExplanation.text: A router is used to determine the path that the messages should take through the network. A firewall is used to filter incoming and outgoing traffic. A DSL modem is used to provide Internet connection for a home or an organization.

questions.prompt: Why would a Layer 2 switch need an IP address?

options.text: to enable the switch to send broadcast frames to attached PCs
to enable the switch to function as a default gateway
to enable the switch to be managed remotely
to enable the switch to receive frames from attached PCs

summary.text: A pure Layer 2 switch forwards frames using MAC information without needing its own IP address for that forwarding.

concept.text: A pure Layer 2 switch forwards frames using MAC information without needing its own IP address for that forwarding. An SVI address allows IP-based management; multilayer switches can have additional routing roles.

rationale.text: Broadcast forwarding at Layer 2 does not require a management IP address.
A pure Layer 2 switch is not made into an IP router simply by assigning a management address.
Remote IP-based management needs a reachable IP endpoint on the switch.
Receiving and switching ordinary Ethernet frames does not require the switch to have a management IP address.

commonMistakes.text: Layer 2 switching does not need the switch management IP.

sourceExplanation.text: A switch, as a Layer 2 device, does not need an IP address to transmit frames to attached devices. However, when a switch is accessed remotely through the network, it must have a Layer 3 address. The IP address must be applied to a virtual interface rather than to a physical interface. Routers, not switches, function as default gateways.

questions.prompt: Refer to the exhibit. An administrator is trying to configure the switch but receives the error message that is displayed in the exhibit. What is the problem?

options.text: The entire command, configure terminal, must be used.
The administrator is already in global configuration mode.
The administrator must first enter privileged EXEC mode before issuing the command.
The administrator must connect via the console port to access global configuration mode.

summary.text: The > prompt identifies user EXEC mode.

concept.text: The > prompt identifies user EXEC mode. Enter enable to reach privileged EXEC before configure terminal; an unambiguous abbreviation such as config t is valid there.

rationale.text: The abbreviation can be valid in the correct mode; spelling it out does not solve the privilege-mode problem.
Global configuration would show a prompt such as Switch1(config)#, not Switch1>.
The command is being entered at user EXEC; privileged EXEC is the required next step.
Authorised remote terminal sessions can also enter configuration mode; console access is not uniquely required.

intro.text: Read the whole prompt to identify the current mode before entering the next command.

practicalExample.code:
Switch1> enable
Switch1# configure terminal
Switch1(config)#

sourceExplanation.text: In order to enter global configuration mode, the command configure terminal, or a shortened version such as config t, must be entered from privileged EXEC mode. In this scenario the administrator is in user EXEC mode, as indicated by the > symbol after the hostname. The administrator would need to use the enable command to move into privileged EXEC mode before entering the configure terminal command.

questions.prompt: What term describes a network owned by one organization that provides safe and secure access to individuals who work for a different organization?

summary.text: An extranet provides controlled access to selected organisational resources for external partners.

concept.text: An extranet provides controlled access to selected organisational resources for external partners. It describes the access relationship rather than a specific hosting technology.

rationale.text: This is the partner-access arrangement described.
Cloud refers to a resource-delivery model; it does not specifically mean authorised access for another organisation.
BYOD concerns using personally owned devices.
QoS concerns traffic treatment and priority, not partner access permissions.

sourceExplanation.text: The term extranet describes a controlled and private network infrastructure owned by a single organization that is purposely built to grant secure, limited access to external individuals who work for completely different organizations or business entities. An extranet is typically deployed to facilitate seamless collaboration with external stakeholders such as trusted suppliers, vendors, business partners, or high-priority clients. It allows them to access specific internal resources and files safely without exposing the core corporate network to broader security risks.

questions.prompt: What term describes storing personal files on servers over the internet to provide access anywhere, anytime, and on any device?

summary.text: Cloud storage keeps files on remotely accessible service infrastructure.

concept.text: Cloud storage keeps files on remotely accessible service infrastructure. Access still depends on connectivity, authentication, service availability and supported clients; the wording is not an unconditional guarantee.

rationale.text: This is the intended remote-storage model.
BYOD describes personal-device use, not where files are stored.
QoS manages traffic treatment, not the storage location.
A converged network carries multiple service types such as voice, video and data; it does not define cloud storage.

sourceExplanation.text: The term cloud (or cloud computing) refers to the practice of storing, managing, and processing data on remote servers hosted on the Internet, rather than on a local hard drive. This architecture allows users to seamlessly upload and retrieve their personal files, applications, and services from any geographical location, at any given time, and across any internet-enabled device.

questions.prompt: What term describes a network where one computer can be both client and server?

summary.text: In a peer-to-peer arrangement a device may request services as a client and offer services as a server.

concept.text: In a peer-to-peer arrangement a device may request services as a client and offer services as a server. This contrasts with the dedicated-server arrangement used in the next comparison.

rationale.text: Peers can provide and consume services without requiring a dedicated central server.
Cloud describes resource provision, not specifically equal peer roles.
BYOD describes device ownership and permitted access.
QoS describes prioritisation and service treatment, not client/server roles.

sourceExplanation.text: The term peer-to-peer (P2P) describes a network model where every interconnected computer can function as both a client and a server simultaneously. In this specific architecture, there is no requirement for a centralized or dedicated server. For instance, a computer acts as a server when it shares a local file or a connected printer with other users, and at the same time, it operates as a client when retrieving a shared document stored on another workstation.
